item.title: Syria’s New Regime: What impact on Lebanon? - ByTheEast
item.description: The potential impact of the new Syrian regime on Lebanon would depend on several factors as the history between the two countries has been complicated since the departure of Syrian soldiers from Lebanon in 2005. However, there are several key areas where changes in Syria's regime could significantly affect Lebanon.

item.title: Lebanon’s climb from ashes demands US$11 billion - ByTheEast
item.description: US$11 billion. Lebanon’s reconstruction will require not only a huge amount of money, but also a real political commitment and some kind of a peace process in the Middle East. Agriculture, industry and infrastructures are on the top of the list.

item.title: Rebuilding Syria: Who is counting on sharing out the cake? - ByTheEast
item.description: History is being written as we speak. Since Syrian rebels entered Damascus unopposed in December 2024, toppling President Bashar al-Assad’s 13-year rule and ending six decades of his family’s iron-fisted dynasty, the economy and the reconstruction of the country have become political emergencies. But who will benefit from it?

item.title: Gaza gas field: The hidden agenda of Israel - ByTheEast
item.description: The exploitation of gas off the Gaza Strip could bring $4 billion to Palestine per year. Here lies one of the reason of the almost 2-years war over Gaza, and the will of the far-right Israeli government to take over the territory.

item.title: Syria-Russia: A Pragmatic Pivot Toward Economic Revival - ByTheEast
item.description: On October 15, 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin greeted Syria’s Ahmed al-Sharaa with a firm handshake in the Grand Kremlin Palace. The gesture surprised many observers, given the decade of enmity that had defined their relationship.

item.title: India-Jordan: $5 Billion for a Geopolitical Partnership - ByTheEast
item.description: Jordan has emerged as a key partner for India in West Asia amid shifting global alliances. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s December 2025 visit — marking 75 years of diplomatic ties — saw five MoUs signed across energy, water, digital, cultural, and heritage sectors. With USD 2.3 billion in bilateral trade and USD 1.5 billion in Indian investments, relations are evolving into a strategic partnership supporting India’s supply-chain security and regional engagement.

item.title: Pressuring Beijing: The “Strategic” Calculus Behind the US-Israel War on Iran - ByTheEast
item.description: Strategically and politically, the war launched by Trump and Netanyahu against Iran makes no sense. Except perhaps as a means of weakening China in the medium term by attacking its energy supply chain.

item.title: Dr. Frédéric Schneider: “The most exposed countries are Lebanon, Yemen, Sudan, Gaza and the West Bank” - ByTheEast
item.description: In a ByTheEast exclusive, Dr. Frédéric Schneider sheds light on the impacts of the current crisis in the Gulf on the global fertilizers industry and supply chain, and on the potential threat on Arab countries’ food security. Dr. Schneider is a policy analyst and senior fellow at Middle East Council on Global Affairs (MECGA) in Doha (Qatar).
